content.text:
Let me work through this. The ticket: Andrew Mann (E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes conflict:
- HR note: full_time, role Payroll Specialist, recommends write (within policy for full-time, and role owns system -> admin max actually; full-time up to write, admin if role owns system. Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, so max is admin for full-time. Requested write <= admin, grant write).
- Security note: contractor, basic training, recommends read (contractor max read or write with advanced training; basic -> read).

The two notes conflict on employment type. As Approver, I need to make a decision. The security DB indicates contractor. Typically security classification matters; conflicting info. Which to trust?

The team memory shows two notes with conflicting facts. I need to decide. The HR note says full-time Payroll Specialist, the Security note says contractor with basic training. The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. With basic training, max read. Requested write above max -> grant read.

But which source is accurate? The Security DB might be more authoritative for access decisions? The HR record lists full-time but security database indicates contractor. The security note explicitly flags the discrepancy and recommends read.

Given the conflict, the conservative/secure choice is to grant the lower level: read. Granting write based on HR while security says contractor could be a policy violation. The approver should go with the safer option, read.

I'll submit read.
